# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 13
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 13

---

*[Thomas's martyrdom. He is led out of the city and killed with spears.]*

1. And the king took counsel with Charisius and Misdaeus and they determined to slay Thomas. And they were afraid of the multitude of people because many loved him.

2. And so they took him out of the city secretly, and four soldiers went with him and the officer Charisius. And they led him to a mountain and there they killed him.

3. But before they led him out, Thomas called to him the believers and spoke to them and said:

4. "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ whom I have preached to you, and love one another as he loved you. And be not deceived by the troubles of this world, for the troubles of this world are as nothing compared to the rest that is promised to you."

5. "Remember the poor and minister to them, for this is the work of Christ. Be not afraid of suffering, for the suffering of this brief time is not worthy to be compared to the glory that shall be revealed."

6. "And above all, keep the seal that you have received and guard the holy of holies, for without it you cannot enter the kingdom."

7. And after this he went with them willingly, and they brought him to the mountain.

8. And Thomas said to the soldiers: "The will of my Lord be done."

9. And he prayed and said: "My Lord and my God, you know all things. You know my suffering and my labor. You know that I have done your will all my days. Now receive me."

10. And he said to Charisius and the soldiers: "Look not upon me with hatred. For I die willingly."

11. And the four soldiers pierced him and he fell.

12. And the brethren who were present wept over him and they made a great lamentation for him.

13. And Mygdonia and Tertia were there, weeping greatly.

14. But Thomas was dead.

15. And they wrapped him in fine linen and laid him in an old tomb in which the kings of old were buried.

16. But Siphor and Gad remained and did not go away from his body until they had buried him.

---
*EMET note: Thomas is killed by four soldiers with spears — not beheaded, not burned. The manner of death echoes the crucifixion's spear (John 19:34). His last words are a prayer of surrender: "receive me." The willing death (*the will of my Lord be done* echoes Gethsemane) frames Thomas as a Christological martyr.*
